docs.title: Documentation
docs.intro: How training is organised in the app, and what each term means. The first four — session, cycle, stage and program — nest inside one another: each groups the one before it.

sections.title: Session
points: One training day: the exercises you do in one go.
Within the cycle they're named in order: A, B, C…
The letter tells you when it comes up, not what it is: reorder them and they're reassigned.

sections.title: Cycle
points: The group of sessions that repeats over and over. In training theory, the microcycle.
If you train A, B and C, the cycle is A-B-C; finish it and it starts again at A.
It usually matches the days you train in a week.
It moves on once you complete ALL of its sessions, not when the week ends.
Order doesn't matter, and repeating a session doesn't count twice.

sections.title: Stage
points: A stretch of the program with one goal: build volume, gain strength, peak. In training theory, the mesocycle.
You build it from a cycle and the number of times you want to repeat it.
Four cycles of A-B-C are A-B-C, A-B-C, A-B-C, A-B-C.
Once you complete them the app tells you, but it never jumps to the next one on its own.
Stages are what let a program evolve instead of repeating the same thing forever.

sections.title: Program
points: The complete plan from start to finish: all of its stages together. In training theory, the macrocycle.
Only one is active at a time.
The rest are archived and you can bring them back whenever you want.

sections.title: Block
points: Conditioning work driven by the clock instead of sets.
AMRAP: most rounds in a time cap.
EMOM: one task per minute.
For time: a fixed amount of work, as fast as possible.

sections.title: Superset
points: Two or more exercises chained with no rest between them.
The rest is taken after the last one in the chain.

sections.title: Dropset
points: Extra sets after the last working set, dropping the weight without resting.
They add volume.
They don't count towards PRs or progression.

sections.title: Progression
points: The rule that sets the weight for your next session.
Automatic: goes up when you hit the target.
Fixed: always the same increment.
Submaximal: a percentage of your max.

sections.title: RPE
points: Perceived effort from 1 to 10.
How many reps you'd have left in the tank.
RPE 8 means roughly 2 reps in reserve.

sections.title: 1RM
points: Your estimated maximum for a single rep.
It isn't measured by lifting it: it's calculated from your sets.

sections.title: PR
points: A personal record on an exercise.
More weight, more reps at the same weight, or more volume than in any previous session.

trainer.title: Trainer
trainer.connectedSub: They send you programs and see the sessions you complete from them.
trainer.pendingSub: Your last session hasn't reached them yet. It retries when you open the app, or you can retry now.
trainer.offSub: If you train on your own you don't need this. Connect only if a trainer writes your programs.
trainer.rowProgramSub: If they update it, the app tells you and you choose when to switch.
trainer.rowProgramNoneSub: They haven't sent you a program yet.
trainer.rowLastUploadSub: Sent on its own after every session.
trainer.rowLastUploadFailed: Failed on {{when}}. It will retry automatically.
trainer.rowAccessGoogleSub: You can restore the connection on another phone without asking your trainer for anything.
trainer.rowAccessCode: You sign in with a code
trainer.rowAccessCodeSub: The code never expires or changes: it's always the same one. Save it so you can get back in if you change phones or reinstall the app.
trainer.sharedBody: The sessions you complete from the programs they send you, plus any free sessions you log after you connected.
trainer.notSharedBody: Programs you built yourself, or anything you trained before connecting.
trainer.retrySub: Try to send your history right now.
trainer.linkGoogleSub: So you don't depend on the code if you change phones or reinstall.
trainer.changeSub: You'll enter the new trainer's code. The current program is archived and theirs arrives instead.
trainer.disconnectSub: You stop sending sessions. Their program is archived and your previous one comes back. Same code to come back.
trainer.disconnectBody: You'll stop sending them your sessions. Their program will be archived and your previous one restored, if you had one. You can reconnect later with the same code.
trainer.how1Sub: It lands in the app and you train with it like any other.
trainer.how2Title: Your sessions reach them on their own
trainer.how2Sub: After every session the log is sent so they can see how you're doing.
trainer.how3Sub: Eight characters like XK7M-2P4T, given to you by your trainer. It's always the same one, so save it: you'll need it if you reinstall the app.
trainer.googleCtaHint: Only if you were connected before and linked your Google account: it restores the connection without typing the code again.
trainer.googleSearching: Looking for the trainer connection linked to your Google account…
trainer.googleNoSlot: That Google account has no saved connection. Ask your trainer for the code.
trainer.expoGoNote: Google doesn't work in Expo Go. Try the installed app.
trainer.errNoIdToken: Google didn't return the account identity. Try again.
trainer.codeLead: Type the code your trainer gave you. It's eight characters like XK7M-2P4T; the dash is added for you.
trainer.codeAlreadyLinked: You're already connected to a trainer. Continuing disconnects you from them and connects you to this one.
trainer.codeHistoryProgramSub: The trainer's program is imported. The history on this phone doesn't change.
trainer.codeHistoryMergeSub: Also restores the history your trainer has stored. Repeated sessions aren't duplicated.
trainer.codeImplies1: Your current program is archived and your trainer's is loaded.
trainer.codeImplies2: Your trainer will see the sessions you complete from their programs.
trainer.codeImplies3: If they change the program, the app tells you and you choose when to switch.
trainer.codeImplies4: Your previous history isn't deleted, and isn't sent to them.
trainer.linkLead: Link your Google account to restore the connection with your trainer on another phone without asking them for the code again.
trainer.linkImplies1: Your trainer connection and your history stay exactly as they are.
trainer.linkImplies2: On another phone, just sign in with Google.
trainer.linkImplies3: You won't have to keep any code.
trainer.linkErrBody: Couldn't link the Google account. Try again.

sync.title: Sync
sync.selectLead: Choose how the app should keep your clients. You can change this later.
sync.modeGoogleDesc: Your clients are tied to your account. There's no code to keep: you sign in with Google and that's it.
sync.modeCodeDesc: The app creates a 12-character code. Everything works the same, but that code is your only key.
sync.modeCodeWarn: Keeping it is on you: without that code the account can't be recovered.
sync.modeOfflineDesc: Nothing leaves this phone. You share programs and history by exporting and importing files by hand.
sync.onlyInstalled: Installed app only, not Expo Go.
sync.warnCodeExists: You already have a code. Creating another one stops your current clients from syncing with it.
sync.warnUpgrade: Your current clients move to your Google account on their own.
sync.nameHint: This is the name your clients see on the programs you send them.
sync.reauthGoogleLink: Sign in with a different Google account →
sync.statusSub: With your personal code. Keep it: it's what gives the account back if you change phones.
sync.reauthHint: Use it if the app stopped recognising you: it signs in again with the code you already have.
sync.revealLead: This is your code. Copy it and keep it somewhere safe: it's the only way to recover the account.
sync.revealWarn: If you lose the phone and don't have the code, the account and the sync with your clients can't be recovered.
sync.recoveryLink: Already have a code? Recover account →
sync.reauthLink: Sign in again with another code →
sync.recoveryLead: Type your trainer code to get your clients back. It's twelve characters; the dashes are added for you.
sync.switchBody: The current account will be signed out. Your clients stay on this phone, but stop syncing until you sign in again.
sync.switchUpgradeBody: Your current clients move to your Google account on their own and you stop depending on the code.
sync.errNoIdToken: Google didn't return the account identity. Try again.
sync.errReconnectBody: Check your code and try again.

drive.title: Drive backup
drive.offSub: Your data lives only on this phone. If you lose it or reinstall the app, it goes with it.
drive.activeSubNever: No backup has been saved yet.
drive.reconnectSub: Google expired the permission. Reconnect the account to keep saving backups.
drive.how1Sub: Programs, history, your own exercises, settings, and also your clients and session templates, in a "Forma Backups" folder on your Google Drive.
drive.how2Sub: The app can only see the files it creates itself; the rest of your Drive is invisible to it.
drive.how3Sub: Each backup is a file with its date. Past 30, the oldest ones are deleted automatically.
drive.expoGoNote: Google sign-in doesn't work in Expo Go. Try the installed app (EAS build).
drive.freqSessionSub: Recommended: the backup is always current and needs no background permissions.
drive.freqDailySub: In the background, even if you don't train that day.
drive.freqWeeklySub: In the background, even if you don't train that week.
drive.freqMonthlySub: In the background, even if you don't train that month.
drive.nameHint: The date is added automatically, so you can tell your backups apart in Drive.
drive.backupNowSub: Don't wait for the next session.
drive.deleteAllSub: They're deleted from your Drive and can't be recovered.
drive.disconnectSub: No new backups are saved. The ones already in Drive are kept.
drive.backupsHint: Tap a backup to restore it on this phone.
drive.backupsEmpty: There are no backups in your Drive yet.
drive.backupsNeedConnect: Connect your Google account in the Settings tab to see your backups.
drive.errExpiredBody: Reconnect your Google account to keep saving backups.
drive.restoreBody: Everything you have in the app right now (programs, history and settings) is replaced by what was in the backup from {{when}}. This can't be undone.
drive.deleteAllBody: They'll be deleted from your Google Drive and can't be recovered. The app stays connected and will save new ones.
drive.disconnectBody: No new backups will be saved. The backups already in your Drive are kept and you can reconnect whenever you want.

beginner.label: Beginner
beginner.description: Less than 1 year training or returning after a long break.
beginner.detail: Machine-guided exercises, basic bodyweight and dumbbell patterns. Simple and safe progression.

intermediate.label: Intermediate
intermediate.detail: Dumbbells, cables, kettlebell and technical bodyweight exercises like pull-ups or dips. Double progression.

advanced.label: Advanced
advanced.description: 3+ years with solid technique in free movements.
advanced.detail: Barbell, weighted exercises, periodization. Requires good technique in squat, deadlift and press.

standard.label: Standard
standard.description: Hypertrophy and general strength. The most complete and versatile approach.
standard.detail: Covers all movement patterns with the best exercises for each goal.

calisthenics.label: Calisthenics / Functional
calisthenics.description: Bodyweight, grip and core. With transfer to sports and aerial disciplines.
calisthenics.detail: Pull-ups, dips, L-sit, hollow body. Relative strength and body control.

glutes_legs.label: Legs & Glutes
glutes_legs.description: Maximum emphasis on glutes, hamstrings and legs. Popular in female programs.
glutes_legs.detail: Hip thrust, Romanian deadlift, leg press and squat variations as central exercises.

strength.label: Strength / Powerlifting
strength.description: Move more weight. Squat, deadlift and press as the core.
strength.detail: 3–6 rep ranges, long rests and load progression as priority.

full_body.label: Full Body
full_body.description: All muscle groups in each session. 2–6 days.

upper_lower.label: Upper / Lower
upper_lower.description: Upper body one day, lower the next. 2 distinct sessions.

push_pull_legs.label: Push / Pull / Legs
push_pull_legs.description: One push day, one pull day, one legs day. 3 sessions.

hypertrophy.label: Hypertrophy
hypertrophy.description: Build muscle mass. 8–12 reps per set.

strength.label: Strength
strength.description: Move more weight. 5–8 reps, long rests.

bodyweight.label: Bodyweight only
bodyweight.description: No equipment — exercises using just your body.

none.label: No limitations
none.description: I can do any exercise without restrictions.

shoulder.label: Shoulder / Trapezius
shoulder.description: Discomfort in shoulder, rotator cuff or trapezius.

lower_back.label: Lower back
lower_back.description: Problems in the lower back area.

double_progression.label: Double progression
double_progression.description: Reach max reps → increase weight → return to min. The most common.

linear.label: Linear progression
linear.description: Add a fixed weight each session. Classic in strength programs like Starting Strength.

reps_progression.label: Rep progression
reps_progression.description: Weight stays the same, only reps increase each session.

upperLowerOptions.2sessionsDesc: A (upper) + B (lower). Simpler, repeat the cycle.
upperLowerOptions.4sessionsDesc: A1 + B1 + A2 + B2. More exercise variety per cycle.
